problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨4,-2,3⟩+w⟨5,-1,2⟩,\,Π:r=⟨10,-5,12⟩+s⟨4,3,0⟩+t⟨0,2,5⟩.
$$
worked_solution:
From the equation of a plane in the parametric form $r=p+tv+sw$, we have that its normal vector is $n=v\times w.$ In our case, the normal vector to $Π$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =⟨4,3,0⟩\times ⟨0,2,5⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 4 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}4 & 3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =15i-20j+8k \\  & =⟨15,-20,8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane $Π$ in dot product form is

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨15,-20,8⟩ & =⟨10,-5,12⟩\cdot ⟨15,-20,8⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨15,-20,8⟩ & =346.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨4,-2,3⟩+w⟨5,-1,2⟩$ into the equation of the plane in dot product form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨15,-20,8⟩ & =346 \\ ⟨4+5w,-2-w,3+2w⟩\cdot ⟨15,-20,8⟩ & =346 \\ 15(4+5w)-20(-2-w)+8(3+2w) & =346 \\ 60+75w+40+20w+24+16w & =346 \\ 111w & =222 \\ w & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $q$ of the intersection point $Q,$ we substitute $w=2$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =⟨4+5(2),-2-(2),3+2(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨14,-4,7⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $Q(14,-4,7).$
